stem: Use the bars to build a data set of ${=n}$ values whose mode is ${=t}$. Any data set with that mode counts.
solution: The mode is the value that occurs most often, so the target value has to appear more times than any other value. Being in the set is not enough.
Raise two of the bars to the target value, so it occurs twice.
Fill the remaining bars with values that are different from the target and different from each other, so that none of them occurs as often as the target.
Check the live readout: the mode shows the target on its own, with no tie.
notes: Builds the part of this objective that the registered misconception is about: a data set made to fit a STATED mode. no-mode is the student who places the target once among all-different values; multi-modal is the student who lets other values repeat as often as the target. Both are the same registered error (mode-not-most-frequent), listed no-mode first as the likelier build. off-target is deliberately NOT mapped: for ask:mode it also fires when the target is absent altogether or when a different single value is the mode, which is a mixed bag. The other error that fires it (target present but outranked by another value) is also this misconception, so a later pass could add off-target if Samuel accepts that residual. Targets are 2-7 (never 0, where a zero-height bar looks like a missing bar); n 5-7 stays inside the instrument's 3-8. The anchor questions of this objective are all mean questions; none uses a mode, so the parent is the objective's simplest anchor (ex10-2-11).
